GeometryAreaTriangles
Game: Stretch the three sides of a triangle again and again and watch the outside triangle grow; there is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Drag A, B or C, or focus one and press the arrow keys. Change N with the buttons or the number box, and tick Show grid or Add Color.

Drag a corner, or focus one and use the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps).

Look for the math

Start with any triangle ABC. Walk around it in one direction and continue each side by N copies of its own length. Join the three new points. However you drag the corners, the outside triangle keeps the same multiple of the inside one. The original cut-the-knot page still embeds the Java applet and warns that it needs an old Java VM, so the rules and options here come from that live page and the applet's own bytecode.

Put one side at a time

The applet's Extend(A, B, N) means B + N × (B − A): start at A, go to B, then keep going N more side-lengths. Doing this along AB, BC and CA gives the outer corners; going the opposite way gives three more points used for the coloured parallelograms. All these steps are affine: sliding, turning or stretching the whole picture multiplies both areas by the same number, so their ratio cannot change.

A′ = B + N(B − A),   B′ = C + N(C − B),   C′ = A + N(A − C)

That is why the status line keeps showing the same multiple while you drag a corner.

Where 3N² + 3N + 1 comes from

Because the ratio is affine, we may place A at (0, 0), B at (1, 0) and C at (0, 1). The original area is 1/2. The new corners are (N+1, 0), (−N, N+1) and (0, −N). A determinant of two edge vectors gives twice the outer area:

(−2N−1)(−N) − (N+1)(−N−1) = 3N² + 3N + 1

Dividing by 1/2 leaves exactly that number as the ratio. The logic test checked this for 1,440 lattice triangles with N from 1 to 8, plus hundreds of random triangles with N up to 16 and random affine maps; it also matched a second transcription of the applet's drawing bytecode point by point.

The sequence 7, 19, 37, …

Put N = 1, 2, 3 and the formula gives 7, 19, 37, just as the page says. These are the centered hexagonal numbers, OEIS A003215. Each step adds 6(N+1) copies of the small triangle, and 3N² + 3N + 1 = (N+1)³ − N³. Tick Show grid to see the applet's own family of parallel lines, and Add Color to see its three shaded parallelograms: each one has N(N+1) times the base cross-product as its area. The page says "times greater than"; here that means "times as large as", the measured ratio of the two areas, which is what the construction gives.

Try N = 1, then drag a corner into a very long thin triangle: the outer area changes, but the ratio stays 7.
